security_audit.summary: Most detections are false positives from Markdown formatting, documentation links, and marketing-analysis language. One command instruction invokes a local ledger utility with a campaign placeholder that is not demonstrably passed through a structured argument interface. The skill explicitly treats exported files as untrusted input and requires confirmation before saving results.

remediation.issue: The ledger command includes a campaign placeholder in a shell-style invocation.
remediation.suggestion: Invoke the ledger utility through a structured argument API, validate campaign identifiers against an allowlist, and avoid interpolating user-provided values into shell commands.

content.value_statement: Paid campaigns can drift from their planned spend curve before teams notice. This skill compares exported spend data with the flight plan and reports a clear pacing decision.
actual_capabilities: Compares cumulative campaign spend with an even, front-loaded, or back-loaded target curve.
Classifies pacing as on-track, ahead, behind, or stalled.
Calculates percent-to-pace and projects end-of-flight spend from the current rate.
Checks whether a campaign remains in its learning phase before recommending action.
Separates measured export data, user-provided values, and estimated projections.
Produces a reallocation trigger and a next-check date for the campaign.
limitations: Requires a campaign export with spend by day and a defined budget and flight window.
Does not set the initial budget, select a bid strategy, or calculate a new allocation.
Does not replace platform reporting, billing records, or professional financial advice.
Pacing conclusions depend on the accuracy and freshness of the supplied export.

use_cases.title: Daily spend review
use_cases.description: Check whether an active search campaign is spending evenly across a monthly flight.

use_cases.title: Launch monitoring
use_cases.description: Review a new social campaign without changing budget while the platform is still learning.

use_cases.title: Client pacing update
use_cases.description: Prepare a clear pacing status and next-check date from an exported campaign report.

prompt_templates.title: Basic pacing check
prompt_templates.prompt: Check pacing for Campaign X. The daily budget is $200. It is day 9 of a 30-day flight. Cumulative spend is $1,650. Use an even target curve.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate overspend
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this campaign export for over-delivery. The lifetime budget is $12,000, the flight runs June 1 to June 30, and the target curve is front-loaded. State the pace gap and likely driver.

prompt_templates.title: Learning-phase safeguard
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess pacing for this campaign, but first confirm whether it is in learning phase. Do not recommend a reallocation while learning is active.

prompt_templates.title: Portfolio-ready handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the attached daily spend export against this back-loaded flight plan. Label each value as measured, user-provided, or estimated. Return the pacing verdict, trigger decision, and handoff summary.

output_examples.input: A $6,000 campaign has spent $2,700 after 10 of 30 days on an even curve.
output: Trigger: Hold if within the agreed band; otherwise review reallocation after learning exits.

output_examples.input: A campaign has spent 30% of its budget with 60% of its flight elapsed.
output: Observed gap: Spend is below the target curve.
Next step: Review delivery status, bid constraints, audience size, and dayparting.

best_practices: Set the target curve and acceptable pacing band before reviewing current spend.
Use recent native-platform exports instead of dashboard screenshots or one total.
Treat a learning-phase pacing read as observational until learning has exited.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a single cumulative spend total as sufficient pacing evidence.
Do not move budget during learning phase solely because of a short-term gap.
Do not present a projected end-of-flight total as measured spend.

faq.question: What data do I need?
faq.answer: Provide a campaign export with daily spend, the budget, the flight dates, and the intended target curve.

faq.question: Can it use a daily or lifetime budget?
faq.answer: Yes. It can assess pacing for either budget type when the flight window is available.

faq.question: Does it change campaign budgets?
faq.answer: No. It identifies whether reallocation should be reviewed and routes allocation work to a separate skill.

faq.question: What is percent-to-pace?
faq.answer: It is cumulative actual spend divided by expected cumulative spend at the same point in the flight.

faq.question: Why does learning phase matter?
faq.answer: Budget changes during learning can reset optimization, so pacing results are observational until learning has exited.

faq.question: Can it save results for later?
faq.answer: Yes, but it asks for confirmation before saving a pacing summary or open follow-up.
